oneLiner: 阴、阳离子通过静电作用结合，常见于活泼金属与活泼非金属。
oneLinerEn: Electrostatic attraction between ions; typical of active metals with active nonmetals.
detail: 阴、阳离子靠静电作用结合成离子键，这种作用既有吸引也有排斥，最终达到平衡；它一般形成于活泼金属与活泼非金属之间。如 NaCl 中钠失去一个电子成 Na⁺、氯得到一个电子成 Cl⁻，两者都达到 8 电子稳定结构。离子键没有方向性也没有饱和性，一个 Na⁺ 周围可同时吸引六个 Cl⁻，所以 NaCl 是立方的离子晶体而不是一个个 NaCl 分子，化学式只表示离子的个数比。据此可判性质：熔沸点较高、硬而脆，固态时离子被钉住不能移动故不导电，熔融或溶于水时电离出自由离子才导电。它与靠共用电子的「共价键」正好相对，二者同属「化学键」，而电负性差越大越倾向生成离子键（见「电负性与电离能」）。
detailEn: Ions are held by electrostatic action that balances attraction and repulsion, typically between a reactive metal and a reactive nonmetal: in NaCl sodium loses one electron to Na⁺ and chlorine gains one to Cl⁻, both reaching a stable eight. The ionic bond has neither direction nor saturation, so one Na⁺ grips six Cl⁻ at once, which is why NaCl is a cubic crystal rather than separate molecules and the formula only gives the ion ratio. Hence the properties — high melting point, hard but brittle, non-conductive as a solid because the ions are locked, yet conductive when molten or dissolved once free ions appear. It is the give-and-take counterpart of the shared-electron covalent bond (see Covalent Bond), both being chemical bonds (see Chemical Bonds), and a larger electronegativity gap favors ionic character (see Electronegativity & Ionization).

oneLiner: 原子间共用电子对形成的化学键，分极性与非极性。
oneLinerEn: Shared electron pairs between atoms; polar or nonpolar.
detail: 原子间通过共用电子对形成的化学键叫共价键，多见于非金属原子之间。按共用电子对有没有偏向，分两类：同种原子间电子对不偏移，为非极性键（H₂、Cl₂、N₂）；不同原子间电子对偏向电负性大的一方，为极性键（HCl、H₂O）。共用一对叫单键、两对叫双键（O=O）、三对叫三键（N≡N），键长依次缩短、键能依次增大。分子整体有没有极性还得看空间构型：CO₂ 虽含极性键却因直线对称而抵消、是非极性分子。电子式用点标出共用与孤对电子，结构式用一根短线代表一对共用电子。共价键有方向性和饱和性，与无方向的「离子键」互补，二者统称「化学键」，成键类型由电负性差决定（见「电负性与电离能」）。
detailEn: A covalent bond is a shared electron pair between atoms, most often nonmetals. If the pair sits evenly the bond is nonpolar (H₂, Cl₂, N₂); if it leans toward the more electronegative atom the bond is polar (HCl, H₂O). One shared pair is a single bond, two a double (O=O) and three a triple (N≡N), with shortening length and rising bond energy. Whether the whole molecule is polar is a separate question of shape: CO₂ has polar bonds yet is a nonpolar molecule because its linearity cancels them. Dot formulas mark shared and lone pairs, structural formulas draw each pair as one line. Covalent bonds are directional and saturated, complementing directionless ionic bonds (see Ionic Bond); together these are chemical bonds (see Chemical Bonds), and the electronegativity gap decides which forms (see Electronegativity & Ionization).

oneLiner: 金属阳离子与自由电子间的强烈作用，赋予金属导电、导热与延展性。
oneLinerEn: Cations in a sea of delocalized electrons; gives conductivity, malleability and luster.
detail: 金属键没有方向性也没有饱和性：金属阳离子排成阵列，价电子脱离各自的原子，变成在整个晶体里自由移动的「电子海」，靠这份共有电子把阳离子们黏在一起。正因为键不挑方向，金属受外力时原子层可以相对滑动而键不断开，这就是延展性——砸成薄片、拉成细丝都靠它；而金刚石这类共价晶体受力时键被强行掰向错误的方向，直接碎裂，所以硬而脆。导电与导热都由那群自由电子负责：加电场就定向移动，受热就加速并把能量传给相邻离子，所以金属的导电性随温度升高而下降（晶格振动加剧、阻碍电子），这与半导体正好相反。自由电子还能吸收并随即放出可见光，于是金属有金属光泽。键的强弱主要看两件事：能给出几个价电子、离子半径多大。碱金属只有一个价电子而半径又大，所以钠能用小刀切开、汞在常温就是液体；过渡金属价电子多、半径小，键强熔点高，钨能撑到 3400 ℃ 以上而用作灯丝。合金通常比纯金属硬，因为掺进来的异种原子大小不一，打乱了本来可以整齐滑移的层（钢比铁硬、青铜比纯铜硬都是这个原因）。
detailEn: A metallic bond has neither direction nor saturation: the cations sit in a lattice while the valence electrons leave their parent atoms and drift through the whole crystal, and this shared sea of electrons is what holds the cations together. Because the bond does not care which way it points, a hammered metal lets its layers slide past one another without breaking anything — that is malleability and ductility — whereas a covalent solid such as diamond has its bonds wrenched into the wrong geometry and simply shatters, hard but brittle. The same free electrons carry current and heat, so a metal conducts better when cold: warming sets the lattice vibrating and scatters the electrons, the opposite of what happens in a semiconductor. Absorb light and re-emit it and you have the metallic lustre. Strength turns on two things, how many electrons are contributed and how small the ion is. Alkali metals give one electron from a large radius, so sodium is cut with a knife and mercury is liquid at room temperature, while transition metals give more from a smaller radius, hence tungsten above 3400 °C and its life as a lamp filament. Alloys are usually harder than the pure metal because atoms of an unequal size disturb the orderly sliding of the layers — steel over iron, bronze over copper.

oneLiner: 分子间的弱作用（范德华力）与较强的氢键，决定熔沸点与溶解性。
oneLinerEn: Weak van der Waals forces and stronger hydrogen bonds govern boiling points and solubility.
detail: 分子之间存在比化学键弱得多的作用：广泛存在的范德华力，以及特殊的氢键。范德华力随相对分子质量增大、分子接触面积增大而增强，所以卤素单质从 F₂、Cl₂ 的气态到 Br₂ 液态、I₂ 固态，熔沸点一路升高；它不是化学键，破坏它只改变物质状态而不改变分子本身。氢键则是含 N、O、F 的分子里，氢与电负性大原子之间的较强吸引，比范德华力强却仍远弱于「共价键」。氢键解释了几件反常：水的沸点远高于同族的 H₂S、冰因氢键把分子排成疏松结构而密度比水小、所以浮在水面、DNA 双链靠碱基间 A–T 与 G–C 的氢键配对。它们与把原子拧在一起的「化学键」分属不同层级的作用，也正是这些弱作用决定了「晶体类型」里分子晶体的低熔沸点（见「晶体类型」）。
detailEn: Between molecules act forces far weaker than bonds: the universal van der Waals force and the special hydrogen bond. Van der Waals grows with molecular mass and contact area, so the halogens climb from gaseous F₂ and Cl₂ to liquid Br₂ and solid I₂ with steadily rising melting and boiling points; it is not a chemical bond, and breaking it changes only the state, not the molecule. A hydrogen bond is the stronger pull, in molecules holding N, O or F, between a hydrogen and an electronegative atom — sturdier than van der Waals yet far weaker than a covalent bond (see Covalent Bond). Hydrogen bonding explains several anomalies: water boils far above H₂S below it, ice floats because hydrogen bonds hold it in an open lattice less dense than liquid water, and the DNA helix pairs A–T and G–C through it. These sit at a different level from the chemical bonds that weld atoms together (see Chemical Bonds), and such weak forces are exactly what give molecular crystals their low melting points (see Crystal Types).

oneLiner: 离子晶体、分子晶体、原子晶体与金属晶体，性质差异悬殊。
oneLinerEn: Ionic, molecular, covalent-network and metallic crystals differ greatly in properties.
detail: 按构成微粒与微粒间作用力，晶体分四类。离子晶体由阴、阳离子经离子键堆成（NaCl、CaO），熔沸点较高、硬而脆，固态不导电而熔融或溶解导电；分子晶体由分子经分子间作用力（有时还有氢键）排列（干冰、冰、碘），熔沸点低、多数易升华、不导电；原子晶体（共价晶体）由原子经共价键向空间延伸成骨架（金刚石、晶体硅、SiO₂），是四类里最硬、熔点最高的；金属晶体由金属阳离子与自由电子经「金属键」结合，导电导热、有延展性。比较熔点大体是原子晶体高于离子晶体高于分子晶体，同类之内再比键强与晶格能，如金刚石硬于晶体硅、MgO 熔点高于 NaCl。晶体类型与化学键类型相互对应，判类型先问微粒、再问作用力（见「离子键」「共价键」）。
detailEn: Sorted by their building particles and the forces between them, crystals fall into four kinds. Ionic crystals stack cations and anions by ionic bonds (NaCl, CaO): fairly high melting, hard but brittle, non-conductive solid that conducts when molten or dissolved. Molecular crystals pack molecules held by intermolecular forces and sometimes hydrogen bonds (dry ice, ice, iodine): low melting, many sublime, non-conductive. Network covalent crystals extend atoms through covalent bonds into a giant framework (diamond, crystal silicon, SiO₂), the hardest and highest-melting of the four. Metallic crystals bind cations and a sea of free electrons by metallic bonds, so they conduct heat and electricity and can be drawn out (see Metallic Bond). Melting points run roughly network above ionic above molecular, and within a kind you compare bond strength and lattice energy, so diamond beats silicon and MgO beats NaCl. The crystal type maps onto the bond type — first ask what the particles are, then what holds them (see Ionic Bond and Covalent Bond).

oneLiner: 元素在化合物中的结合能力，正负化合价代数和为零。
oneLinerEn: Combining power of an element; the sum of oxidation numbers in a neutral compound is zero.
detail: 化合价是原子的结合能力，本质是成键时电子偏移的数目：离子化合物里等于得失电子数（NaCl 中钠 +1、氯 −1），共价化合物里等于共用电子对的数目与它的偏向（H₂O 中氢 +1、氧 −2）。用起来只有三条硬规矩和一张常查表。规矩一：单质里元素的化合价为 0，因为不存在电子偏向谁的问题。规矩二：化合物里正负化合价的代数和为 0，这是求未知价态的万能钥匙——知道钾 +1、氧 −2，就能从 KMnO₄ 推出 Mn 为 +7、从 K₂MnO₄ 推出 +6、从 MnO₂ 推出 +4。规矩三：同种元素在不同物质里可以取不同价，甚至在同一物质里同时取两种价（Fe₃O₄ 里铁是 +2 与 +3 混合，平均 +8/3），所以「铁有可变化合价」必须落实到具体物质上说。初中要求背下的常见价态口诀是：一价氢氯钾钠银，二价氧钙钡镁锌，三铝四硅五价磷，二三铁、二四碳，二四六硫都齐全，铜汞二价最常见，单质为零。化合价还直接决定两件事：写化学式时的交叉法，以及氧化还原的判断——化合价升高就是失电子、被氧化、作还原剂，降低则相反，这个口径与「氧化还原反应」一条完全一致，不要与「化合反应」混为一谈。
detailEn: Valence is an atom's combining capacity, and underneath it is simply the number of electrons that shift when a bond forms: in an ionic compound it equals the electrons lost or gained (sodium +1, chlorine −1 in NaCl), in a covalent one the count of shared pairs and which way they lean (hydrogen +1, oxygen −2 in water). Three hard rules carry the whole topic. Rule one: an element in its free state is zero, since nothing is leaning anywhere. Rule two: the algebraic sum in a neutral compound is zero, the master key for any unknown — knowing potassium +1 and oxygen −2, manganese comes out +7 in KMnO₄, +6 in K₂MnO₄ and +4 in MnO₂. Rule three: one element may take several valences, and within a single substance even two at once (Fe₃O₄ holds both +2 and +3, averaging 8/3), so variable valence is always stated substance by substance. The chant learned at thirteen runs: hydrogen, chlorine, potassium, sodium and silver one; oxygen, calcium, barium, magnesium and zinc two; aluminium three, silicon four, phosphorus five; iron two and three, carbon two and four; sulphur two, four and six; copper and mercury most often two; free elements zero. Beyond that, valence dictates how a formula is crossed out and, in the redox chapter, who was oxidised: a rise means electrons lost, the substance oxidised and acting as the reducing agent, and the reverse for a fall — the same wording kept throughout the redox entry, and never to be confused with a synthesis reaction.

term: 电子式与 8 电子稳定结构
termEn: Electron-Dot Diagrams and the Octet Rule
oneLiner: 用点把最外层电子摆出来，既看清成键也看清是否满足稳定结构。
oneLinerEn: Dot the outer shell and you see both the bonding and whether a stable arrangement was reached.
detail: 电子式是用小黑点标出最外层电子的图，中学阶段它同时干三件事：表示微粒、表示成键、表示反应过程。规则不多但要分家看。离子化合物的电子式要写出方括号与电荷，阳离子直接把符号与电荷写在外面（Na⁺ 不必画点，因为它的最外层已在上层），阴离子要带方括号并把八电子画满（[Cl]⁻ 周围八点），NaCl 的电子式就是一个钠离子挨着一个氯离子方括号；共价化合物不加方括号、不写电荷，共用的一对电子摆在两原子中间，孤对电子一律画全（H₂O 除两根 O—H 还要留两对孤对）。书写过程用箭头表示电子去向：钠与氯形成 NaCl 是钠把一个电子交给氯（离子键，见「离子键」），氢与氯形成 HCl 是双方各出一个电子共配对（共价键，见「共价键」），两条箭头写法不同正对应两种键。判「是否满足 8 电子」有条快捷公式：对 ABₙ 型分子，中心原子的「|化合价| + 最外层电子数」等于 8 就满足——CO₂ 中碳 4+4=8 满足，SO₂ 中硫 4+6=10 不满足，PCl₅ 中磷 5+5=10 不满足，BF₃ 中硼 3+3=6 也不满足；氢永远只能凑到 2 电子，所以 HCl 里的氢与 H₂ 都按 2 电子判。几个特殊微粒必须单独记：NH₄⁺ 是四个 N—H 共价键加整体带正电的方括号，其中一个是配位给予（见「配位化合物」）；OH⁻ 有孤对又带电荷；Na₂O₂ 与 CaC₂ 里存在 O—O 与 C≡C 的原子团，画成单个离子就会漏键；稀有气体是单原子、八点独立，这也是它们不活泼的图示化解释（见「元素周期律」）。最集中的三类错误：漏画孤对电子（把 CO₂ 画成 O=C=O 而不标点，或氨少画一对）、把共价化合物加上方括号（HCl、H₂O、CO₂ 一律不加）、以及把离子化合物的电荷写进方括号内。考试还常问「某分子所有原子是否都满足 8 电子」，判法是把氢先剔掉再看其余：NH₃ 里氢只到 2，所以「所有原子都满足 8 电子」对它是错的；PCl₃ 与 CCl₄ 才对。电子式与结构式的分工也别忘了：电子式管电子，结构式一根短线代表一对共用电子、只表示连接顺序，二者对同一分子不能混用（见「化合价」）。
detailEn: An electron-dot diagram marks the outer-shell electrons as dots, and at this level it does three jobs at once: depict a species, depict a bond, depict the forming of one. The rules divide by class. An ionic compound is drawn with brackets and charges: the cation needs no dots (sodium's outer shell has been surrendered and the next one down is already complete), while the anion sits in brackets with its eight dots filled in — so sodium chloride is one sodium symbol beside a chlorided bracket. A covalent molecule takes no brackets and no charges; the shared pair goes between the two atoms and every lone pair is drawn (water shows two O—H pairs plus two lone pairs on oxygen). Formation is shown with an arrow tracing the electron: sodium giving one electron to chlorine for NaCl (ionic), hydrogen and chlorine each contributing one to pair up for HCl (covalent) — the arrows differ precisely because the bonds differ. Testing the octet has one shortcut. For ABₙ the centre satisfies the octet when |valency| plus its outer-electron count equals eight: in carbon dioxide 4 + 4 works, in sulfur dioxide 4 + 6 does not, nor does 5 + 5 in PCl₅, and BF₃ leaves boron at 3 + 3 = 6. Hydrogen can never reach past two, so HCl and H₂ are judged on the duet. Several species must be memorised separately: ammonium is four N—H covalent bonds inside a charged bracket, one of them a donated pair (see coordination compounds); hydroxide carries both a charge and lone pairs; sodium peroxide and calcium carbide hold O—O and C≡C groups that vanish if you draw bare ions; the noble gases stand as single atoms with eight free dots, which is the picture of their inertia (see the periodic law). Three errors dominate the mark schemes: omitting lone pairs (ammonia drawn with one pair short), putting brackets round a covalent molecule (never for HCl, water or carbon dioxide), and writing the charge inside the bracket for an ionic anion. The question 'does every atom here reach eight?' is answered by removing hydrogen first: ammonia fails because its hydrogens hold only two, whereas PCl₃ and CCl₄ pass. Finally separate the dot diagram from the structural formula — dots are about electrons, a stroke is one shared pair and shows connectivity only; for a given molecule the two must not be conflated (see valency).

term: 极性分子与非极性分子
oneLiner: 键有没有极性看电负性差，分子有没有极性还得看构型对不对称。
oneLinerEn: Bond polarity comes from an electronegativity gap; molecular polarity also needs the shape to be asymmetric.
detail: 这是两级判断，混在一起就必错。第一级判键：同种原子之间电子对不偏向，为非极性键；不同原子之间电子对偏向电负性大的一方，为极性键（判据与程度见「电负性与电离能」）。第二级判分子：把各键的极性按空间构型做矢量叠加，抵消得了就是非极性分子，抵不掉就是极性分子。所以「含极性键的分子不一定是极性分子」：CO₂ 两根 C=O 都是极性键，但直线形对称而抵消；CH₄ 四根 C—H 极性很弱却因正四面体完全对称而是非极性分子；CCl₄ 同理。反过来「只含非极性键的分子一定非极性」（H₂、O₂、N₂、P₄），而「极性分子里可以只有极性键」（HCl、H₂O、NH₃）。判构型要靠「分子空间构型（VSEPR）」那条，实操上有个粗糙却好用的口诀：中心原子没有孤对电子的常常对称（CO₂、BF₃、CH₄ 都非极性），有孤对电子的常常不对称（NH₃ 三角锥、H₂O 角形、SO₂ 角形都极性）——但这是经验而非定理，最终以矢量图为准。分子极性直接决定溶解性，这就是「相似相溶」：极性溶质易溶于极性溶剂，非极性溶质易溶于非极性溶剂。因此碘几乎不溶于水却易溶于四氯化碳与酒精（碘酒的配制、碘水中加四氯化碳振荡后分层、上层近无色下层紫红，是萃取的标准例子，分离办法见「分离与提纯的方法及仪器配套」），油污要靠汽油或四氯化碳洗而不用水，NaCl 溶于水却不溶于汽油。它也影响沸点：极性分子之间除范德华力还多一层偶极吸引，所以相对分子质量接近时丙酮与水的沸点高于非极性的同类（分子间作用的整体口径见「分子间作用力与氢键」）。还影响化学性质：水是极性分子，所以它是最常见的溶剂、能电离出 H⁺ 与 OH⁻ 而参与大量离子反应；四氯化碳不燃且比空气重，历史上被用在灭火剂里（它遇明火会分解出光气，现在已被禁用）。课堂验证极性与否有一张经典图：酸式滴定管分别装水与四氯化碳放成细流，把摩擦过的玻璃棒靠过去，水流明显偏转、四氯化碳流几乎不动——一个把分子当小磁针的思路，直观却只作定性。判断顺序永远写成三步：先看键的极性，再看空间构型是否对称，最后才给分子定性。
detailEn: Two judgements run in series; merging them is the usual way to lose the mark. First the bonds: between like atoms the shared pair does not lean, so the bond is non-polar; between unlike atoms it leans toward the more electronegative one, so the bond is polar (the criterion and its scale sit under electronegativity and ionisation energy). Then the molecule: add the bond dipoles as vectors over the actual geometry, and whatever cancels leaves a non-polar molecule, whatever survives leaves a polar one. Hence a molecule with polar bonds need not be polar — both C=O bonds in carbon dioxide are polar yet the linear shape cancels them, and the four weakly polar C—H bonds of methane cancel perfectly in a tetrahedron, as do those in carbon tetrachloride. Conversely a molecule built only from non-polar bonds is certainly non-polar (H₂, O₂, N₂, P₄), while a polar molecule may contain polar bonds only (HCl, water, ammonia). The geometry itself is worked out under VSEPR; a rough but serviceable rule of thumb says that a centre with no lone pair is often symmetric (carbon dioxide, BF₃, methane — non-polar) while one with a lone pair is usually not (ammonia's pyramid, water's and sulfur dioxide's bent shapes — polar). It is a rule of thumb: settle it with the vector picture. Polarity decides solubility, which is the like-dissolves-like rule. Iodine barely dissolves in water but readily in tetrachloromethane and ethanol — the basis of iodine tincture and of the standard extraction where shaking iodine water with tetrachloromethane gives a colourless top and violet bottom (separations are tabulated in the quick reference); grease lifts with gasoline, not water; sodium chloride dissolves in water but not in gasoline. It lifts boiling points too, since polar molecules add a dipole attraction to the dispersion force, so acetone and water run above non-polar peers of similar mass (the general account is under intermolecular forces). It shapes chemistry as well: water being polar is the commonest solvent and ionises enough to feed countless ionic reactions, while non-polar, heavy, non-flammable tetrachloromethane was once used on fires until its decomposition to phosgene over flame got it banned. The classroom test turns molecules into compass needles: run fine streams of water and of tetrachloromethane from burettes, bring a rubbed rod near each, and the water stream veers while the other barely moves — qualitative, but persuasive. Fix the order of work: bonds first, symmetry second, the molecule's polarity last.

term: 化学键与分子间作用的破坏
oneLiner: 溶、熔、汽化各拆掉哪一层作用，判据完全不同，别只想着「断键」。
oneLinerEn: Dissolving, melting and vaporising tear different layers apart; do not assume a bond always breaks.
detail: 物质的三态变化与溶解，动的其实是不同层次的作用，把它们一律说成「破坏化学键」是这一块最集中的错法。先把层级排好：分子内的化学键（离子键、共价键、金属键）强，分子间的作用（范德华力、氢键）弱，两者相差常常一个数量级。于是判断就落在两问上——这物质由什么微粒构成、微粒之间靠什么结合。冰融化、酒精挥发、碘升华，破坏的都只是分子间作用与氢键，分子本身完好，所以碘蒸气仍是 I₂；而氯化钠熔化或溶于水，离子键被拆开、离子自由移动，因此能导电；二氧化硅（石英）与金刚石熔化要断共价键，所以熔点极高而导电性始终不行；金属熔化破坏金属键，自由电子仍在，故液态金属照样导电。溶解这一栏最容易错，须逐个抠：蔗糖、酒精溶于水只破坏分子间作用，溶液以分子存在故不导电；NaCl、KNO₃ 溶于水破坏离子键并电离；HCl、H₂SO₄ 溶于水时破坏的是共价键，靠水的作用电离出离子——共价化合物却在水中导电，这是「化合物导电与否看电离不看键型」的典型；NaHSO₄ 溶于水既拆离子键又拆共价键（电离出 Na⁺、H⁺ 与 SO₄²⁻），所以它既是钠盐又是酸式盐；Na₂CO₃ 溶于水只拆离子键，CO₃²⁻ 保留完整，正因如此它才有水解的余地（见「盐类水解」）。判据里还藏着两条常考对比：熔化时能导电的化合物一定是离子化合物（有自由离子），熔化时不导电而常温溶于水电离的多是共价化合物（HCl 型），因此「测熔点导电」可用来区分 NaCl 与 HCl 这类物质。化学变化与物理变化的分界同样落在这里：只有旧键断裂与新键生成的才是化学变化，所以 NaCl 溶于水虽拆了离子键却没有新键生成，中学一般仍把它归作物理—化学之间的溶解过程而不写成化学反应；而 2Na + 2H₂O 生成碱与氢气既断旧键又成新键，毫无疑问是化学变化。最后提醒一句最常被反问的：水的三态变化中，氢键与范德华力一起被削弱，所以冰浮在水面、水的沸点在同族氢化物里异常地高（见「分子间作用力与氢键」）；而「汽化时化学键被破坏」这种说法对分子晶体一定错，对原子晶体（金刚石、石英、晶体硅）却也不成立——它们熔化才断键，常温下根本不汽化。把晶体类型先定下来（见「晶体类型」），再谈破什么作用，顺序就不会错。
detailEn: Changes of state and dissolving act on different layers, and calling every one 'breaking chemical bonds' is the most concentrated error in this topic. Set the layers first: bonds inside a molecule — ionic, covalent, metallic — are strong, the forces between molecules — dispersion and hydrogen bonding — are weak, commonly by an order of magnitude. Judgement then reduces to two questions: what particles is this substance built from, and what holds them together? Melting ice, evaporating ethanol, subliming iodine disrupt only intermolecular attraction and hydrogen bonds; the molecules stay whole, which is why iodine vapour is still I₂. Sodium chloride, melted or dissolved, has its ionic bonds pulled apart and its ions set free, so it then conducts. Silica and diamond must snap covalent bonds to melt — hence their enormous melting points and their permanent failure to conduct. Molten metal loses its metallic bonds but keeps its electron sea, so a liquid metal conducts as readily as a solid. Dissolving is where the mistakes cluster, so take it species by species. Sugar and ethanol go into water as molecules, having surrendered only intermolecular attraction, and their solutions do not conduct. NaCl and KNO₃ give up ionic bonds and ionise. HCl and sulfuric acid break covalent bonds as they dissolve, ionising under water's action — a covalent compound conducting in water, the standing proof that conduction depends on ionisation, not on bond type. Sodium hydrogensulfate loses both ionic and covalent bonds, yielding Na⁺, H⁺ and sulfate, which is exactly why it is both a sodium salt and an acid salt. Sodium carbonate loses only its ionic bonds and keeps CO₃²⁻ intact — hence its readiness to hydrolyse (see salt hydrolysis). Two comparisons hide inside the criteria: a compound that conducts when molten must be ionic, since free ions are required, while one that is inert at the melting point yet ionises in water is typically covalent (the HCl case), so testing conductivity at the melt separates NaCl from HCl. The chemical-versus-physical boundary lands here too: only where old bonds break and new ones form is there a chemical change, so dissolving NaCl, which severs ionic bonds but forms none, is not written as a reaction at this level, whereas sodium on water, breaking and forming together, unquestionably is. One question comes back every year: in water's own changes of state, hydrogen bonds and dispersion forces weaken together, which is why ice floats and why water boils absurdly high among its group hydrides (see intermolecular forces and hydrogen bonding). And 'vaporising breaks the chemical bonds' is always wrong for a molecular crystal — nor does it ever apply to diamond, quartz or silicon, which only break bonds on melting and never vaporise at room temperature at all. Fix the crystal type first (see crystal types), then discuss which force gives way; in that order the answer stays correct.
